name: flying-button
title: Flying Button
description: A rounded charcoal call-to-action reading Launch project, with two little engine pods beneath it. The recording only shows it at rest; the code is built to lift it on a jet of smoke when hovered.
use: A playful launch or submit button on a marketing page that can afford a moment of theatre.
avoid: The button leaves its place and hides the cursor, so it is a poor fit for touch or critical forms.
a11y: The label stays a real button with a focus ring, but liftoff is hover-driven and the cursor is hidden while flying. (keyboard: partial, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A long dark-charcoal pill with softly rounded ends sits centred on black, the white label inside and a faint light sheen across its top edge. Two small grey tabs poke out beneath the lower rim like tiny engine nozzles.
behaves: In every frame the button stays still: the pointer moves onto it and the hand cursor appears, but nothing lifts and no smoke or flame is emitted. In the source, hovering is meant to fire thruster columns and fly the button upward, carrying a drawn cursor with it.
customise: Pass the label as children and set size, theme, radius, altitude, hover time, jet count, trigger mode and the optional ramp track. Thruster, smoke, button and text colours are props too.
weight: heavy: A grid fluid simulation runs advection, pressure and dye passes plus a smoke shader each frame.
